title: Universal Driven Critical Dynamics of Entanglement Entropy
authors: Chang-Yu Shen, Shuai Yin, Zi-Xiang Li
abstract: The Kibble-Zurek mechanism (KZM) and finite-time scaling (FTS) provide a foundational framework for driven critical dynamics, yet their predictive power has been largely confined to local observables. Here, we establish a universal finite-time scaling theory for the nonequilibrium dynamics of quantum entanglement. Using unbiased quantum Monte Carlo simulations, we investigate the corner entanglement entropy of (2+1)-dimensional interacting Dirac fermions driven from ordered phases toward a quantum critical point. We find that the corner entanglement accurately obeys a universal driven scaling governed by the driving rate and system size, persisting whether the initial ordered state is fully gapped or hosts gapless Goldstone modes. Crucially, this dynamical entanglement exhibits a logarithmic dependence on the driving rate, from which the universal corner coefficient of the underlying conformal field theory can be robustly extracted far from equilibrium. These results generalize the KZM from local observables to the intrinsic nonlocal quantum information measures, offering a practical blueprint for characterizing quantum criticality and entanglement on programmable quantum simulators.
summary: This research establishes a universal finite-time scaling theory for quantum entanglement entropy in driven quantum systems. By analyzing the corner entanglement entropy of Dirac fermions, the authors show that the scaling behavior robustly reveals the universal corner coefficient of the underlying critical theory. This extends critical dynamics concepts from local measurements to intrinsic, non-local quantum information measures.
main_problem: The paper aims to extend the predictive power of Kibble-Zurek and finite-time scaling from local observables to non-local quantum information measures, specifically quantum entanglement entropy, in driven critical dynamics.
main_result: The corner entanglement entropy exhibits a universal finite-time scaling governed by the driving rate, allowing the robust extraction of the underlying conformal field theory's universal corner coefficient far from equilibrium.
method: The authors use unbiased Quantum Monte Carlo simulations, employing an incremental algorithm to calculate the corner entanglement entropy ($\Delta S_2$) for various driving rates.
model_or_system: The study investigates interacting Dirac-fermion models, including the Hubbard and spinless t-V models, on honeycomb and pi-flux square lattices, driven across quantum critical points (QCPs).
key_observables: Corner Entanglement Entropy ($\Delta S_2$), which is used to probe the universal scaling behavior.
important_parameters: The driving rate ($R$), system size ($L$), and the characteristic scaling variable ($RLr$).
main_assumptions: The analysis assumes the system remains within the low-energy scaling window ($a \ll \xi_R \ll L$) for the asymptotic scaling function to hold.
figures_summary: Figures illustrate the calculation of $\Delta S_2$ via lattice cuts and show data collapse when plotting $\Delta S_2$ against $\ln R$ or $\ln(RLr)$ for different system sizes.
paper_structure: The paper establishes the theoretical framework connecting FTS to entanglement, applies it to specific fermionic models, details the numerical implementation using incremental algorithms, and finally extracts the universal QCP corner coefficient by analyzing the scaling function's asymptotic behavior.
why_interesting: This work provides a powerful, non-local diagnostic tool—entanglement entropy—to characterize quantum criticality in driven systems, which is highly relevant for understanding non-equilibrium dynamics in quantum simulators.
